sections.history: Yogananda Narasimha lies about two kilometres south-east of Lower Ahobilam, where the plain meets the first folds of the Nallamala hills, and is one of the nine Narasimha shrines that make up the Ahobilam pilgrimage. It is among the most accessible of the nine, reached by a motorable road, and pilgrims usually visit it together with Chatravata Narasimha, which stands on the same route. The shrine is maintained within the Ahobila Matha's worship of the nine forms, and its structure is generally associated with the Vijayanagara period, when the temples of Ahobilam were richly endowed.
sections.architecture: A small walled temple with a pillared mandapa leads to the sanctum, where Narasimha sits cross-legged in a posture of yoga, the conch and discus in his upper hands. The image is serene rather than fierce: the leonine face is calm and the body is gathered inward, so that the shrine feels, in essence, like a place of meditation.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that after Hiranyakashipu was slain and the Lord's fury had subsided, Narasimha instructed Prahlada here in yoga, the disciplines that still the mind; hence Yogananda, bliss in yoga. The young prince who had held firm through every torment thus became the Lord's pupil. In the astrological reading of the nine shrines, Yogananda Narasimha is linked with Saturn.
sections.festivals: Narasimha Jayanti and the annual Brahmotsavam of Ahobilam are the principal occasions; Saturdays draw devotees who associate the shrine with Saturn. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: This is a peaceful shrine and an easy one: a road leads close to the gate, so it suits elderly pilgrims and families. Sit for a while after darshan — the image invites stillness. Visit it with Chatravata Narasimha on the same short outing from Lower Ahobilam.

visit.timings: Worship is offered daily with morning and evening darshan and a midday closure. Confirm current timings locally.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Lower Ahobilam is reached by road via Allagadda; Nandyal is the nearest major railhead. Yogananda Narasimha is about two kilometres south-east of Lower Ahobilam by road; autos and jeeps are available locally.
